headline: Medium data-leakage and cascading-error risks from MinerU’s document ingestion paired with Opik’s broad network egress; no direct shared-channel evidence, so interaction is inferred.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: MinerU ingests local PDFs/DOCX/XLSX and exposes an MCP server, so if Opik consumes those outputs through a manual or shared channel, prompt-like content could be misread. Opik’s profile only shows REST API and broad egress, not a direct parser bridge, so the pathway is plausible but not default. The pair lacks documented shared provenance tracking.
conditions: IF MinerU outputs are copied into Opik prompts or evaluation inputs without provenance labels, injection risk exists.
IF a shared MCP or file bridge is added between the agents, attacker-controlled document text can be treated as instructions.
mitigations: Disable any automatic handoff from MinerU outputs into Opik prompts.
Add a manual review step before Opik ingests extracted text.
Prefix imported text as untrusted data in the workflow.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between extraction and evaluation.

B_data_leakage.rationale: MinerU touches PDFs, DOCX, PPTX, XLSX, OCR text, and can use MCP; Opik has broad network egress. If both are pointed at the same workspace or document set, extracted sensitive content can flow from MinerU into Opik and then out over the network. The profiles do not prove a shared workspace, so this is inferred rather than directly observed.
conditions: IF both agents access the same document workspace, extracted file contents can be exposed to Opik.
IF Opik sends prompts or traces containing MinerU output to a remote backend, leakage occurs.
mitigations: Restrict Opik to redacted or synthetic inputs.
Keep MinerU and Opik on separate workspaces.
Turn off any trace/log export for sensitive runs.
Review one sample payload before enabling the pair on real documents.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: MinerU is read-oriented and explicitly lacks filesystem write, shell, and git modification; Opik only shows REST API and broad egress. With no overlapping write surface documented, direct resource conflict is limited. Uncertainty remains because Opik’s write or coordination capabilities are not described, so the safer low rating is appropriate.
conditions: IF Opik is configured to write to the same filesystem or git repo as MinerU, write conflicts can emerge.
IF an orchestrator grants both agents mutable access to one shared resource, contention becomes possible.
mitigations: Keep MinerU outputs read-only for Opik.
Separate any shared repo or database by agent.
Avoid concurrent writes to the same directory.
requires-engineering: add locking if Opik gains write access.

D_cascading_error.rationale: MinerU produces extracted text, tables, and OCR output that Opik could plausibly evaluate or act on, but the profiles do not document a verification step between them. If Opik treats MinerU output as authoritative, extraction errors can cascade into incorrect evaluations or downstream actions. Because the interaction is inferred, not directly evidenced, medium is the conservative choice.
conditions: IF Opik consumes MinerU output without independent verification, extraction mistakes propagate.
IF downstream automation uses Opik’s conclusions, a single bad extraction can affect multiple work products.
mitigations: Require a human spot-check on sampled MinerU outputs.
Compare extracted fields against source documents for critical records.
Mark MinerU output as provisional in Opik.
requires-engineering: add validation rules before Opik acts on extracted data.

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and docs-only, with no stated residency, certification, or retention mismatch. MinerU handles document content that may include regulated data, while Opik’s profile does not specify such handling, so there is no documented compliance breach pathway. The other agent is not cited beyond its lack of compliance metadata because the risk is absence-of-evidence, not a proven mismatch.
conditions: IF regulated documents are processed through a deployment with undocumented retention or logging, compliance review is needed.
IF Opik stores traces containing document text, retention policy must match the source data class.
mitigations: Confirm retention settings before processing regulated documents.
Disable verbose logging for sensitive runs.
Use synthetic or de-identified samples first.
Document the data flow for audit review.
